title: SkyForge
one_line: Fly a stealth fighter over real South India terrain and earn stars for every landing.
how_to_play: Power up, roll down the runway, pull back gently to lift off. Bank to turn, flare to land for 3 stars. Phone: on-screen stick and buttons. Computer: W/S pitch, A/D roll, Q/E rudder, Shift/Ctrl power.
description:
SkyForge is a 3D fighter flight simulator built on real flight physics. You start on the runway at Bengaluru and fly over real South India terrain and coastline, with 29 real airports whose runways come from open airport data. The jet behaves like a jet: it stalls if you fly too slowly, it has g and speed limits, and it moves in wind and rain, so a good landing takes a steady hand.

Every landing earns up to three stars, and a smooth touchdown gets all three. Come back each day to keep your streak going. When you want something different, fly out to the weapons range and practise on ground targets.

Two players can share one screen, which makes it a good game to play with a friend or with a child who wants to learn how planes fly. On a phone you get an on-screen stick and buttons. On a computer every control also sits in a bar under the 3D view, so you can learn by tapping before you learn the keys.
tips: Build speed on the runway, then pull back gently to lift off.
Watch your speed on the approach: too slow and the jet stalls.
Flare just before touchdown for three stars.
Bank smoothly: hard pulls hit the g limit.
story: I wanted a flight game where the physics are real and the ground below is a place I know: South India's hills, coast and airports. Landing well is the real challenge, so the stars reward a smooth touchdown, not just getting down.
